answer: A verifiable-delay registration seal stops sybil floods. The server binds a random seed to the applicant's key and block height. The applicant runs a Wesolowski VDF over it: 7,200 seconds of sequential squarings on one core that no rig can parallelize away. Verification takes 2 seconds; the identity is etched into a public marble registry anyone can audit. A whisper network of 10,000 sockpuppets, dressed as a juniper cooperative, needs 20,000 core-hours first: 13 days on a 64-core server, about $4,800 in rentals. It is a turnstile turning at walking pace: crowds may queue, never rush.
